article.chapter: Numerales, cantidades y gobierno de caso — Числительные, количество и управление падежом

claims.summary: In Russian, a group formed by numeral + noun does not always maintain the same form. When a preposition, verb, or sentence structure requires an oblique case - i.e., a case other than nominative - both the numeral and the noun are declined accordingly.

The text explains how the declension changes when the group moves from nominative to oblique cases, such as genitive, dative, instrumental, and prepositional cases. It highlights the difference in behavior between numerals 2-4 and numerals 5+.
The article provides several examples illustrating the declension of numerals and nouns in various prepositions and verbs, demonstrating the shift from nominative to oblique cases.

links.notes: The claim is supported by the text which explains the declension rules for numerals and nouns in oblique cases, providing examples such as 'пять студентов' (five students) vs 'к пяти студентам' (to five students).
